source.title: The generalization error of max-margin linear classifiers: Benign overfitting and high dimensional asymptotics in the overparametrized regime
source.authors: Andrea Montanari; F. Ruan; Youngtak Sohn; Jun Yan

record.file_problem: No substantial text loss or truncation apparent; the text identifies itself as arXiv:1911.01544v3, dated 22 Mar 2023.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives results on max-margin classifier test error as feature dimension, random-feature width, and sample size vary. These results refine or challenge a general double-descent account: some settings show monotone error changes or a classical U shape rather than a peak followed by a second descent.
record.gate_note: Prior findings about double descent cited from other papers are not recorded as results here. The paper's stated max-margin and random-features outcomes, including its qualitative descriptions of plots, are recorded. Numerical plot values are not transcribed where the text does not state them.
record.test_reason: The paper derives exact asymptotic test error, with simulations, for max-margin classifiers in the overparametrized (separable) regime ψ>ψ*. It sweeps random-feature width, sample size and number of included features. These results bear on whether error improves past the interpolation threshold (V4) and whether more data hurts near it (V3). Below ψ* the max-margin classifier is undefined, so the first descent and the threshold peak itself are not studied.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with additions. The authors derive exact asymptotics for max-margin error and margin, and the interpolation threshold. Random-features error decreases monotonically with overparametrization. In the isotropic well-specified model error increases with ψ, which they attribute to target complexity growing with p; they contrast this with min-norm least squares. In the misspecified model adding features helps only up to ψ0. They also give conditions for benign overfitting, and show that overparametrization is necessary for near-Bayes error. Finally, they show the wide random-features limit is equivalent to a soft-margin linear classifier.
record.recipe_differences: The paper derives high-dimensional asymptotics for max-margin linear classifiers on Gaussian features and applies them to a one-layer random-features model with fixed random first-layer weights. It is not a sweep of conventionally trained deep networks like the cited double-descent studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior differs between random-features and isotropic well-specified settings, and between well-specified and misspecified models. Random-features simulations vary activation, β, d, ψ1, and ψ2; the paper states that the matched-activation results are hardly distinguishable.

fits_no_version.finding: The maximum margin increases with ψ while test error falls (random features) or rises (isotropic well-specified). Classical margin-based bounds stay above 1 and have the wrong qualitative ψ dependence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Margin-based generalization bounds do not track test error across overparametrization for max-margin classifiers.

record.problems: The settings are stylized Gaussian max-margin classification and a one-layer random-features model, not standard fully trained deep networks. Some reported comparisons are limited to simulations averaged over 20 instances, and numerical values for several results are available only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant outcome rows omitted. Results cited from prior work in Sections 1 and 4 are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: Deep networks are not studied. Only a one-layer random-features model with a fixed first layer and max-margin readout is analysed. Neither the peak at the interpolation threshold nor the first descent can be measured, because max-margin is undefined for ψ<ψ*.
Crossing the threshold into the non-separable regime, where max-margin is undefined. Sample-size effects in the random-features model.
The underparametrized branch, the classical U-curve, and the peak at the threshold. Only the ψ>ψ* branch is characterised.
Any single effective-complexity measure locating the peak.
Noise-driven peaks, multiple descents, and removal of the peak by optimal regularization. β varies label noise, but every curve stays monotone past ψ*, and no peak is analysed.
Recounting complexity by an effective number of parameters.

missing.what: Theorem 1: the max-margin excess error is at least c·n/p, and is bounded above by bias/variance terms. Overparametrization is necessary for near-Bayes error, and benign overfitting is shown under slowly decaying covariance spectra.
Wide-network limit: as ψ1→∞, random-features max-margin error converges to that of a soft-margin linear classifier. This is an implicit-regularization account of the second descent's asymptote.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is not one of the original sources. Its theory covers only ψ>ψ*, so it cannot show a full fall-rise-fall curve; the monotone decrease in random features is the second-descent branch, not a reversal of V1. The deep-network V1 link was dropped because random features with a fixed first layer is a different system. R10 is the same experiment as R7–R9 read along ψ.

versions.untested_parts: The tested width sweep is a one-layer random-features model with a fixed random first layer and a max-margin readout, not a conventional fully trained deep network; multilayer networks and trained representations are not tested.
Test error over training epochs or training time.
The paper does not report a separate sweep designed to isolate sample-size effects at a peak of a model-wise double-descent curve; its sample-size results are for the stated isotropic settings.
The paper studies max-margin linear classifiers and a random-features model, not a broad empirical survey of all model classes.
Whether one effective-complexity measure predicts the peak location along model size, epochs, and sample size.
Whether label noise or variance drives a double-descent peak, whether multiple peaks arise, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
Whether counting complexity by an effective number of parameters turns second descent into an ordinary U shape.

rows.subject: isotropic well specified model
rows.size_stated: p varies; p = 800 in the preceding isotropic experiment
rows.operation_detail: Vary the overparameterization ratio ψ = p/n and measure test error.
rows.value: The paper states that test error is monotone increasing in ψ for ψ above the interpolation threshold.
rows.note: This is a theoretical and simulation result for isotropic max-margin classification, not a deep-network experiment.
rows.check: This re-reads the R7–R9 data (p=800 fixed, n varied) along ψ. The authors note that in this model raising p also raises target complexity. It is therefore not a capacity sweep at a fixed task, so it qualifies V4 rather than refuting it.

rows.subject: isotropic misspecified model
rows.stage_stated: Max-margin linear classifier using the first p features
rows.operation_detail: Vary the number of included features and measure test error.
rows.value: Test error decreases for ψ between the interpolation threshold and ψ0, then increases for ψ > ψ0.
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors on empirical means of 20 instances; error bars described as barely visible.
rows.note: This is a decrease followed by an increase as features are added, rather than a fall-rise-fall pattern. Numerical values are shown in the figure but not stated in the text.
rows.check: The data distribution is fixed. Error falls between ψ* and ψ0 = 2, then rises once the added features are pure noise. The second descent holds only up to ψ0.

relation.reason: The study derives prediction-error asymptotics and reports simulations under sample-size and feature-width sweeps that directly bear on V3 and V4.

tranche.reason: Appendix L supplies explicit qualifications to V4 and a counterexample to V3 in the tested separable regime: the well-specified isotropic error increases with p/n, while the misspecified model improves only until the signal-bearing features are exhausted.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is the March 2023 arXiv version, despite the record's 2025 publication year. The reported error curves establish behavior on the separable side, without establishing a complete curve across the threshold.

statements.correction: Figure 5: p=800; beta=1,2,8; 20 instances; error decreases as n increases toward separability. Theorem 3(b)-(d): asymptotic results restricted to psi>psi*. No reported continuation of prediction error below psi*. Eq. (1.4): optimization over unit-norm vectors without a positive-margin constraint.
statements.problem: The sample-size result and its conditions are correct. The claim that max-margin is undefined beyond separability overstates the restriction: Eq. (1.4) defines a normalized max-min optimization, while the reported error asymptotics cover only the separable regime.

statements.correction: Nonseparable-side prediction-error continuation: untested. Theorem 3(c): prediction-error asymptotics only for psi>psi*. Eq. (1.4): normalized max-min optimization remains defined without separability; a positive-margin separating classifier is unavailable below the threshold.
statements.problem: Continuation beyond separability is untested here, but the text does not establish that the normalized max-margin optimization is undefined there.
